---
title: "MAUI Blazor App Architecture"
---

This document explains the architecture of a .NET MAUI Blazor Hybrid application.

## File Structure

```
MauiBlazorAppTest/
├── MauiProgram.cs          # App entry point & DI configuration
├── App.xaml(.cs)           # MAUI Application class
├── MainPage.xaml(.cs)      # MAUI page hosting BlazorWebView
├── Components/
│   ├── _Imports.razor      # Global Razor imports
│   ├── Routes.razor        # Blazor Router configuration
│   ├── Layout/
│   │   ├── MainLayout.razor    # Page layout template
│   │   └── NavMenu.razor       # Navigation sidebar
│   └── Pages/
│       ├── Home.razor      # "/" route
│       ├── Counter.razor   # "/counter" route
│       └── Weather.razor   # "/weather" route
├── wwwroot/
│   ├── index.html          # HTML shell for Blazor
│   └── css/                # Stylesheets
├── Platforms/              # Platform-specific code (iOS, Android, Mac, etc.)
└── Resources/              # App icons, images, fonts
```

## How It Works (Layer by Layer)

### 1. Entry Point (`MauiProgram.cs`)

```csharp
public static MauiApp CreateMauiApp()
{
    var builder = MauiApp.CreateBuilder();
    builder
        .UseMauiApp<App>()
        .ConfigureFonts(fonts =>
        {
            fonts.AddFont("OpenSans-Regular.ttf", "OpenSansRegular");
        });

    builder.Services.AddMauiBlazorWebView();  // Registers BlazorWebView

#if DEBUG
    builder.Services.AddBlazorWebViewDeveloperTools();
    builder.Logging.AddDebug();
#endif

    return builder.Build();
}
```

**Key Points:**
- Configures dependency injection container
- Registers the `BlazorWebView` service that bridges MAUI and Blazor
- In Debug mode, adds developer tools and debug logging

### 2. Application Class (`App.xaml.cs`)

```csharp
public partial class App : Application
{
    public App()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
    }

    protected override Window CreateWindow(IActivationState? activationState)
    {
        return new Window(new MainPage()) { Title = "MauiBlazorAppTest" };
    }
}
```

**Key Points:**
- Creates the main application window
- Sets `MainPage` as the root content

### 3. Main Page with BlazorWebView (`MainPage.xaml`)

```xml
<ContentPage xmlns="http://schemas.microsoft.com/dotnet/2021/maui"
             xmlns:components="clr-namespace:MauiBlazorAppTest.Components"
             x:Class="MauiBlazorAppTest.MainPage">

    <BlazorWebView x:Name="blazorWebView" HostPage="wwwroot/index.html">
        <BlazorWebView.RootComponents>
            <RootComponent Selector="#app" ComponentType="{x:Type components:Routes}" />
        </BlazorWebView.RootComponents>
    </BlazorWebView>

</ContentPage>
```

**Key Points:**
- `BlazorWebView` is a native WebView control that hosts Blazor content
- `HostPage` points to the HTML shell file
- `RootComponent` mounts the `Routes` component at the `#app` element

### 4. HTML Shell (`wwwroot/index.html`)

```html
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
    <meta charset="utf-8" />
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0" />
    <title>MauiBlazorAppTest</title>
    <base href="/" />
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap/bootstrap.min.css" />
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/app.css" />
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="MauiBlazorAppTest.styles.css" />
</head>
<body>
    <div class="status-bar-safe-area"></div>
    <div id="app">Loading...</div>
    <script src="_framework/blazor.webview.js" autostart="false"></script>
</body>
</html>
```

**Key Points:**
- Standard HTML page that hosts the Blazor app
- `#app` div is where Blazor components are rendered
- Uses `blazor.webview.js` (not `blazor.server.js` or `blazor.webassembly.js`)

### 5. Blazor Router (`Components/Routes.razor`)

```razor
<Router AppAssembly="@typeof(MauiProgram).Assembly">
    <Found Context="routeData">
        <RouteView RouteData="@routeData" DefaultLayout="@typeof(Layout.MainLayout)" />
        <FocusOnNavigate RouteData="@routeData" Selector="h1" />
    </Found>
</Router>
```

**Key Points:**
- Scans the assembly for components with `@page` directives
- Routes URLs to the correct page component
- Wraps all pages in `MainLayout` by default

### 6. Layout (`Components/Layout/MainLayout.razor`)

```razor
@inherits LayoutComponentBase

<div class="page">
    <div class="sidebar">
        <NavMenu />
    </div>

    <main>
        <div class="top-row px-4">
            <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/aspnet/core/" target="_blank">About</a>
        </div>

        <article class="content px-4">
            @Body
        </article>
    </main>
</div>
```

**Key Points:**
- Defines the overall page structure (sidebar + main content)
- `@Body` is replaced with the current page component
- `NavMenu` provides navigation links

### 7. Pages (`Components/Pages/`)

Example - Counter page:

```razor
@page "/counter"

<h1>Counter</h1>

<p role="status">Current count: @currentCount</p>

<button class="btn btn-primary" @onclick="IncrementCount">Click me</button>

@code {
    private int currentCount = 0;

    private void IncrementCount()
    {
        currentCount++;
    }
}
```

**Key Points:**
- `@page "/counter"` defines the route
- Standard Blazor component with HTML and C# code
- Event handlers like `@onclick` work the same as web Blazor

## Key Concepts

### Hybrid Architecture

MAUI Blazor is a **hybrid** approach:
- **MAUI** provides the native shell (window, lifecycle, platform APIs)
- **Blazor** handles all UI rendering inside a WebView
- **BlazorWebView** is the bridge between these two worlds

### Execution Model

Unlike Blazor WebAssembly which runs .NET in the browser via WASM, MAUI Blazor runs .NET **natively**:
- On macOS/iOS: Uses Ahead-of-Time (AOT) compilation
- The WebView only handles rendering; all .NET code runs natively

### CSS Isolation

Blazor supports component-scoped CSS:
- Create `ComponentName.razor.css` alongside your component
- Styles are automatically scoped to that component
- Compiled into `MauiBlazorAppTest.styles.css`

## Comparison: Blazor Web vs MAUI Blazor

| Aspect | Blazor Web | MAUI Blazor |
|--------|-----------|-------------|
| **Host** | Browser | Native WebView |
| **Script** | `blazor.server.js` or `blazor.webassembly.js` | `blazor.webview.js` |
| **Runtime** | .NET on server or WASM in browser | Native .NET (AOT on iOS/Mac) |
| **Platform APIs** | Limited (browser sandbox) | Full access via MAUI |
| **Deployment** | Web server or static hosting | App store or direct install |

## Benefits of MAUI Blazor

1. **Code Reuse**: Share Blazor components between web and native apps
2. **Native Performance**: .NET runs natively, not in WASM
3. **Platform Access**: Full access to device features (camera, GPS, file system)
4. **Familiar Tooling**: Same Razor syntax, C#, and patterns as Blazor web
5. **Cross-Platform**: Single codebase for iOS, Android, macOS, and Windows
